criteria.description: FB-26: the trail sampler asserts hue lock within 10 degrees, deltaE*ab no greater than 8 against the payload-derived expectation from rampForReturn(holding.dayReturn) (not rampForWeekly / weeklyReturn), and ordering across same-direction holdings - for every holding in the fixture, sampled at each holding's own naturally unoccluded orbital phase. Literal-hex baselines survive only for flat, comet and sun tokens.

implementer.notes: Remediation re-investigation of F2 (review Finding 2), per-ticker as required -- not a restatement of the three-ticker clamp theory. Fresh full independent re-run of the unmodified sampler (150s window) reproduces the same 3/8 pass, 5/8 fail split (GOOG 7.395, IBM 6.674, CRM 7.079 pass; ASML 8.993, COST 9.749, MSFT 8.28, INTC 9.071, CBRS 8.25 fail) -- MSFT/INTC/CBRS's clamp-collision cause (three holdings pinned to the identical brightest ramp stop, additive-glow bleed) stands unchanged from the prior turn and is not re-argued here. ASML and COST each have a distinct, newly-identified, measured cause: ASML -- built a per-frame clearance log (docs/phase10-baseline/section-13/f2-investigation/asml-cost-clearance-frame-log.json) sampling the live trail-sample point every ~0.7s for 16 consecutive frames (~11s): ASML's clearance-to-its-own-planet-disc is NEGATIVE in all 16 frames (-10.75px to -5.38px), i.e. the sample point sits inside ASML's own rendered planet body for a sustained stretch of its orbit, not intermittently. The fresh full 150s sampler run's best-found frame still only reaches 3.783px clearance (docs/phase10-baseline/section-13/raw-trail-sampler-TST-03.json) -- just above the 1px pass floor. A marked crop of that exact authoritative sampled pixel (docs/phase10-baseline/section-13/f2-investigation/asml-sampled-pixel-marked.png) shows the sample marker sitting directly on the boundary between ASML's own planet disc and the sun's corona -- confirming and refining the reviewer's sun-proximity hypothesis: the contamination source is proximity to ASML's own tight-orbit/large-disc geometry (radiusPx ~20.8, one of the largest of the 8, at an orbit radius of only ~80px from the sun -- distanceCenterToSun measured in raw-f2-investigation.json), which structurally leaves too little clearance for any orbital phase to be comfortably unoccluded, rather than the sun's aurora/glow-shell/docking-ring elements specifically (those were checked and ruled out as the direct contact source; ASML's own planet edge is). COST -- ruled out the moon/label/graticule hypotheses directly: raw-f2-investigation.json measures zero overlapping label bounding boxes near COST's sample point, ASML's moon is 194px away, and the graticule ring sits at 1.6-1.66x the OUTERMOST planet's orbit radius (~608-675px from the sun) while COST orbits at ~127px -- nowhere near it. COST's own clearance-to-its-planet is a comfortable ~29-40px (not a self-occlusion case like ASML). The marked crop of COST's authoritative sampled pixel (cost-sampled-pixel-marked.png) shows the marker landing near the trail ribbon's antialiased radial edge rather than centered in its solid/opaque core, unlike IBM's marker (ibm-sampled-pixel-marked.png), which sits squarely in the middle of a wide, evenly-lit ribbon -- consistent with COST's measured signature (hueDistance 0.636 degrees, essentially correct hue, but deltaE driven by lower luminance/chroma from partial ribbon coverage, not a hue-shifting contamination source). Both causes trace to the shared, ticker-invariant TRAIL_SAMPLE_FRACTION=0.62 verification constant (src/lib/observatory/scene-model.ts:26) not guaranteeing a centered, comfortably-clear sample point for every holding's specific orbit-radius/disc-size/camera-obliqueness combination -- it is a verification-methodology characteristic, not a magnitude/ramp/arc-length defect, so MIN_RETURN_MAGNITUDE/MAX_RETURN_MAGNITUDE, the ramp functions, and the arc-length formulas were not touched, per FB-26's explicit scope boundary. Changing TRAIL_SAMPLE_FRACTION or the clearance-search parameters would itself be a design/verification-methodology decision affecting the pass/fail state of the 3 currently-passing tickers without a bounded way to verify no regression within this remediation's scope -- this is the same design-vs-tool conflict FB-03's precedent reserves for the owner, now with genuine ticker-specific evidence rather than the prior turn's single shared theory. Flagging back per the handoff's own instruction rather than resolving unilaterally.

reviewer.notes: Independently read the full evidence file rather than the summary. The implementer's clamp+glow root cause correctly explains 3/5 failures (MSFT/INTC/CBRS, all pinned to the identical brightest ramp stop) but does not explain ASML (dayReturn +6.5%, not clamped, deltaE 8.993) or COST (dayReturn -2.1%, deltaE 10.156, worse than any clamped ticker, vs IBM at nearly identical -2.0% magnitude passing at 6.674). See docs/phase10-workflow/reviews/section-13-review.md Finding 2 for the required per-ticker re-investigation (sun-glow proximity for ASML's inner orbit; unexplained COST/IBM divergence). Does not authorize touching clamps/ramp/arc formulas.

criteria.description: FB-17: --panel-width default changes from 460px to 600px. A capture of the live production default (no query params, real npm run build && npm run start) at 1440x900 shows the panel at 600px, plus a written, measured explanation of the live/capture size disagreement the owner reported, covering panel width measured across a realistic range of viewport widths (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920) and browser zoom as a candidate cause.

implementer.notes: Live production default (npm run build && npm run start, no query params) renders the approach panel at exactly 600px across all five tested viewport widths (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920), all at devicePixelRatio 2. The calc(100vw - 3rem) responsive floor does not bind at any tested width (100vw-3rem >= 1232px, well above 600px), so viewport width alone does not reproduce the owner's live/capture disagreement. Leading remaining candidate per the investigation: non-100% browser zoom, which shrinks the effective CSS pixel viewport the same way a narrower window would but cannot be simulated by Playwright's viewport option. The calc() floor itself was not changed -- it is a genuine constraint, not a bug -- since the investigation did not find a units/precedence defect.

reviewer.notes: Independently re-measured panel width at all five viewports (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920) against a fresh production server: exactly 600px at every width, confirming the calc(100vw - 3rem) floor does not bind in this range, matching the implementer's own finding.

criteria.description: FB-22: a 1440x900 overview capture shows no unexplained yellow/gold haze or glow above the sun, with the implementer's notes naming the actual identified cause among the aurora mesh, the glow shells, or the docking ring.

implementer.notes: Root-caused via live capture and pixel sampling directly above the sun's projected center (not guessed): a vertical pixel scan straight up from the sun found bright yellow/gold values (e.g. rgb(251,229,101), rgb(244,172,77)) 20-100px above the sun's disc edge, matching a visible soft yellow glow bulging above the sphere in the crop. This is the aurora mesh (candidate a) -- at the overview camera's elevated, forward-offset angle, its prior position (yInOuterRadii 0.92, zInOuterRadii -0.72) placed it close enough behind the sun in screen projection to visually merge with its silhouette. Fixed by repositioning it further up/back (yInOuterRadii 1.65, zInOuterRadii -1.35) -- opacity/formula (raised by FB-02 in this same section) was deliberately left untouched since the owner wants the aurora reliably visible, not hidden. Re-captured after the fix: the same vertical scan and crop show a clean sun silhouette with no haze. Not the glow shells (symmetric full-sphere, opacity too low at rest to read as a distinct shape) or the docking ring (hover-only, only visible on interaction, and full 360 degrees rather than a semi-circle).

reviewer.notes: Reviewed a fresh overview capture from a freshly built production server: clean sun silhouette, no yellow/gold haze above it.

implementer.notes: Remediation of review Finding 1 (VIS-10 fail): the active-tab rule (.missionControl nav a[aria-current="page"], orrery.module.css) tied in cascade specificity (0,2,2) with the unconditional .missionControl .missionStrip nav a rule declared later in the file, which won for border-bottom-*. Fixed by re-scoping the active-tab selector to .missionControl .missionStrip nav a[aria-current="page"], raising its specificity to (0,3,2) so it always wins. Also fixed a pre-existing selector bug in this section's own capture-section-13.mjs evidence script (it queried the page's first unscoped 'nav a', which was not Mission Control's tab strip -- corrected to scope the query to '[class*="missionControl"] nav a', matching the reviewer's own script's approach). Verified via live computed style on the actual rendered [aria-current="page"] anchor (not source reading): active tab now resolves borderBottomWidth 2px / borderBottomColor rgb(255,240,207) (cream), inactive tabs resolve borderBottomWidth 1px / borderBottomColor rgba(213,186,140,0.28) -- activeDiffersFromInactive: true. Fresh capture at Mission Control's production default (no query params) visually shows a distinct box outline on the active ORBITS tab only.

reviewer.notes: The orange background is genuinely gone (independently confirmed: backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0) on every tab). But the active tab's intended 2px solid cream border-bottom never renders -- a pre-existing unconditional rule (.missionControl .missionStrip nav a, border: 1px solid rgba(213,186,140,0.28)) ties in specificity with .missionControl nav a[aria-current="page"] and, being declared later in the file, wins the cascade for border-bottom-*. Live computed style on all 8 tabs: borderBottomWidth 1px, borderBottomColor rgba(213,186,140,0.28) -- active and inactive are visually identical, so the 'which tab is open' affordance is missing in the shipped default.
